dependencies: GitHub CLI and authenticated GitHub API access
known_limitations: Recorded runtime session IDs are required but cannot be authenticated against an app-local session tree.

files.capability: Issue-form to canonical body-template heading synchronization sensor
known_limitations: Heading/label order checks do not prove semantic equivalence, GitHub form rendering, or post-creation enforcement.
The static parser checks checkout jobs with explicit job-level permissions; it does not prove inherited permissions, token behavior, or live GitHub policy.

dependencies: authenticated GitHub CLI and interactive TTY for issue submission
known_limitations: Only fixed-enum callers and unguarded ERR-trap failures can offer feedback; deliberate exits, CI, non-TTY runs, missing metadata, or missing GitHub CLI stay silent.
EXIT-trap chaining recognizes only the Bash single-quoted trap shape, and fixtures simulate the TTY/GitHub CLI path rather than proving a live public Issue submission.

dependencies: the five CI control signatures and remediation paths declared by the manifest
known_limitations: Coverage is allowlist-based and currently limited to five exact-line signatures in .github/workflows/ci.yml; new controls or semantically equivalent edits are invisible until the manifest changes.
A stale or incorrectly anchored signature can report misleading drift; the TSV itself performs no validation or enforcement.
It proves only that each anchored text signature is present in a local file; it does not prove that the workflow or control executes or matches live GitHub settings.
Waivers require only a known control ID and non-empty reason, and the sensor reports but never remediates drift.

dependencies: authenticated GitHub CLI with repository and organization read access
GitHub APIs for repository rules, rulesets, Actions permissions and variables, check runs, contents, and organization plans
known_limitations: This is a GET-only point-in-time sensor: it neither persists a profile nor mutates controls, and missing permissions, API failures, or rate limits remain UNKNOWN.

Required-check source binding depends on the latest observed check runs, while merge-queue applicability uses plan metadata and a static workflow-trigger scan; absent or ambiguous evidence remains UNCHECKABLE rather than proving safety.

dependencies: authenticated GitHub CLI with Issue read access
GitHub Task Issue bodies containing exactly one File ownership section
known_limitations: Only literal prefixes before *, ?, or [ are compared; glob semantics, case, symlinks, and filesystem normalization are not resolved, so comparison is intentionally conservative and malformed bodies are UNCHECKABLE.
It compares only the Issue numbers explicitly supplied and does not discover all active Tasks or reserve ownership paths.

dependencies: the five official GitHub Copilot changelog, RSS, and documentation URLs recorded by the baseline
known_limitations: Committed values are aging snapshots that detect byte or GUID/date changes at five selected URLs; they do not establish capability semantics or availability in any runtime.
Regression fixtures overwrite checkpoint values, so they validate schema and consumer behavior but not the freshness or correctness of the committed baseline.

dependencies: authenticated GitHub CLI with Issue read access and Issue write access for --create-issue
known_limitations: Candidate counts treat the filing as occurrence 1 and count only comments whose body starts exactly Occurrence:; they do not verify same-root-cause evidence and can undercount other recorded forms.
Platform checkpoints are network, hash, and RSS change signals at selected URLs rather than product-capability proof; missing tools, redirects, or fetch failures become unknown.
The always-on budget is only a 150-line heuristic for two files, and --create-issue idempotency is based on one open monthly title.

dependencies: an existing target script path to invoke
known_limitations: The file is a thin launcher that accepts any existing script path; all safety, semantics, and output interpretation remain in the invoked shell script.
Regression coverage is structural and non-Windows and does not exercise native-Windows Git Bash discovery or execution.

dependencies: Invoke-WebRequest with TLS 1.2 access to raw.githubusercontent.com
SCAFFOLD_REPO, SCAFFOLD_REF, and SCAFFOLD_SOURCE_DIR environment contract
known_limitations: The PowerShell bootstrap always downloads scaffold-init.sh from the moving main branch without an independent digest or signature; SCAFFOLD_REF affects only the later Bash fetch.
No dedicated native-Windows or hosted-Windows regression validates TLS download, Git Bash discovery, argument forwarding, cleanup, or exit propagation.

dependencies: curl and tar for public network installs
authenticated GitHub CLI for private-source installs or API ref resolution
a source template tree or GitHub commit tarball
known_limitations: Initial install copies every source .github path and upgrade installs absent files in every ownership class, so source-development records can be carried into adopter repositories.

Upgrade ownership is path-classified: engine collisions are overwritten while tuned and instance-document collisions are kept, so project changes inside engine files rely on subsequent Git diff review.
Network content is commit-addressed but not independently signed, and a dirty local source records sha=unknown.

An unresolved SCAFFOLD_REF matching only 7 to 39 hexadecimal characters is accepted as a commit without expansion; the tarball may fetch, but the 40-hex scaffold-version contract records sha=unknown and version-bound feedback stays disabled.

audit_findings.finding: Current two-tier lifecycle is Project conductor -> Epic conductor -> Task supervisor -> isolated PR worker, with durable dispatch/release and a pre-commit small-Task exemption.

Initial install copies all .github files and upgrade installs absent documentation; newly added source-specific ADR/context records therefore leak into adopter truth namespaces despite documentation saying development records belong under root docs and are never installed.

Task ritual validates marker chronology but not runtime session identity, Outcome/Evidence completion, role authorization, worktree isolation, or comment freshness; open Issue #6 tracks external-delegation risk.
Ruleset solo/team profiles and governance sensors exist, but onboarding still invokes the legacy no-profile path and README lacks detailed operator commands claimed by recent changelog text.
run.ps1 has Windows workflow evidence; scaffold-init.ps1 lacks direct native-Windows regression.
Plugin spike is a no-go for replacing repository assets; declarative activation, auto-update, cloud/IDE/app behavior remain unproved.

One public raw plugin spike includes a personal absolute-path example, and two public provenance files declare internal sensitivity. Planning artifacts cite only path/class, never the sensitive string.

ADR-0003 and AGENTS.md define stacked PR mechanics but keep activation off pending post-GA evaluation at #89. Live source #89 is an unrelated closed, unmerged governance PR, so the activation condition is broken or ambiguous and must not be treated as active source parity.
